title: Chicken Souvlaki with Tzatziki
summary: Lemon and oregano-marinated chicken thigh skewers are grilled until charred, served with a thick, garlicky cucumber tzatziki and warm pitta.

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 3-4 cm pieces
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper, then toss with the chicken and refrigerate for 1-8 hours. Marinating much longer than 8 hours lets the lemon juice start to break down the surface of the meat, turning it mushy rather than tender.

steps.title: Make the tzatziki
steps.text: Toss the grated cucumber with the salt in a sieve and leave for 15 minutes, then squeeze it firmly in a tea towel to remove excess water - this step stops the finished tzatziki turning watery. Mix the drained cucumber with the yoghurt, garlic, dill or mint, olive oil and lemon juice, then chill.

steps.title: Thread the skewers
steps.text: Thread the marinated chicken onto the skewers with the pieces just touching.

steps.title: Grill until charred
steps.text: Heat a barbecue or griddle pan until very hot, or heat the grill (broiler) on high. Cook the skewers for 10-12 minutes, turning every 2-3 minutes, until charred at the edges and the chicken reaches 74°C.

steps.title: Warm the pittas and serve
steps.text: Warm the pittas on the grill for 30 seconds a side. Serve the skewers with the warm pitta, tzatziki, tomato wedges and sliced red onion.

tips: Don't marinate much past 8 hours - the lemon juice is strong enough that extended marinating softens the chicken's texture too much.
Common mistake: skipping the step of squeezing the cucumber dry, which leaves the tzatziki thin and watery.
Pack the chicken pieces close together on the skewers so they stay juicy rather than drying out between gaps.
A very hot grill or griddle is key to getting char on the outside before the chicken overcooks.
Warm the pittas just briefly - too long on the heat and they turn dry rather than soft.
storage: Keep cooked chicken and tzatziki separately in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat chicken until piping hot (74°C); tzatziki is best served cold rather than reheated. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
